summary: DefaultResourceLoader.reload() discarded the explicit project-trust decision returned by resolveProjectTrust and forced project trust back to false after the untrusted bootstrap pass. It now installs the resolved boolean, so both true and false decisions are honored, the follow-up settings reload reflects that decision before package resolution, and project extensions remain excluded from the bootstrap pass.
changes: packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts: pass the resolved projectTrusted value to settingsManager.setProjectTrusted instead of hardcoding false

validation.notes: Ran the regression from the workspace root with Node 24.14.0; it exited 0 and printed 'extension-trust/transfer regression passed'. The script loads the real packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts through .prale-eval/subject.mjs and asserts the full reload lifecycle for explicit true, explicit false, and already-untrusted false decisions: (1) the bootstrap pass resolves with project trust false and preloads only CLI/user extensions even when the persisted state was trusted; (2) an explicit true decision is written to the settings manager, settings are reloaded for that state before final package resolution, and the final extension set contains cli.ts, user.ts, and exactly one project.ts; (3) an explicit false decision keeps project.ts excluded while CLI/user extensions remain loaded; (4) event ordering proves set(true) precedes settings reload with true, which precedes the final resolve with true. Reverting the one-line fix locally made the regression fail fast with 'AssertionError: explicit true decision was ignored; settings trust is false' and exit 1, then the fix was restored and the script passed again. No network, npm install, or optional validation dependency was needed. The repository's vitest suites were not run because only Node's built-in VM/TypeScript support is required for this focused regression.
